title: Guidelines For Schools on Setting Criteria for Direct Admission Scheme
what_it_is: Guidelines For Schools on Setting Criteria for Direct Admission Scheme

sections.label: DSA selection query cases
sections.summary: MOE says about seven parents a year query DSA selection outcomes, and reviews found schools selected rigorously, objectively and professionally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Over the past five years, there have been an average of seven cases per year from parents querying the outcome of their child's DSA selection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Based on MOE's review of each case, we have found the schools to have conducted their selection processes rigorously, objectively and professionally.

sections.label: Seven cases versus 4,000 applications
sections.summary: Seven cases out of 4,000 successful applications is a lower percentage than PSLE appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Just to put things into perspective: what is seven cases out of 4,000 successful applications?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That percentage is lower than even the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) appeals.

sections.label: Transparency and objective assessment
sections.summary: A school's proposed field must be communicated transparently to everyone, and the child's potential in that field must be objectively assessable.

sentences.text: First, whichever field or area that the school proposes, it must be communicated transparently to everyone, not just to a sub-group of people, so that anyone who is interested can apply for it.
Second, there must be some ability to objectively assess the potential of the child in that field.

sections.label: Assessing performance, potential, follow-through
sections.summary: A professional panel should objectively assess performance and potential, and selection must be followed through by identifying talent and working with parents.

sentences.text: What we want is not just performance, but potential.
But to the extent that we can, we want a professional panel to make sure that these are assessed objectively, both performance and potential, and that it can stand up to scrutiny.
The third thing that we need to do well for DSA is that, when it comes to the selection process, we must follow through.

This means we must have an upstream process to look at the potential of our children, whether they come from a privileged or less-privileged background, we must be able to identify those talents and work with the parents to continue to develop those talents in the children.
